messages:
ava: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can we get concrete on the new ship rhythm and how oncall handoffs will work for Dedicated customers? I heard 'monthly windows' and 'oncall pairing' but need specifics for my teams.
suman: +1. Also need to know what the quality bar is for canaries — are we gating on error-rate <0.5% and P95 latency <200ms or something else?
jia: From product side: Dedicated SLA target stays 99.9% monthly uptime, but we said we'll update playbooks for canary criteria. I'll share the draft by EOD.
marcus: For oncall: rotation length stays 2 weeks, shadow pairing for first week on new rollouts, primary/backup model remains. Ops will run automated pre-canary smoke with these checks:
- healthcheck pass
- 0 alerts above SEV2 in last 15m
- synthetic P95 < configured threshold
ava: Does that align with the "automatic fallback" promise? If canary fails, is traffic auto-rolled back or do we manual intervene?
marcus: We have automated rollback for model-level regressions (confidence checks + latency spikes). For infra regressions we currently prefer manual rollback with auto-notify. Recommend we add an opt-in for auto-rollback for low-risk flows.
suman: Action: Eng-runtime to propose opt-in toggle and safety thresholds by next Tues.
ava: Thanks — can someone paste the runbook link and add owners for these action items?
marcus: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-and-canary
jia: Owners: Suman (runtime), Priya (platform infra), DevOps Oncall alias for handoffs.
release-bot: deploy 1899991200 to staging succeeded :rocket:
ava: Perfect, will follow up in the roadmap doc. :thumbsup:
suman: I'll add the opt-in PR and tag @ava for review.
